newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Anti-Hanoi group members detained in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Hanoi group members detained in Cambodia.

text.p: Twenty-eight ethnic Vietnamese, including a U.S. citizen, were detained by Cambodian authorities for belonging to an anti-Hanoi group and for trying to enter Thailand illegally, an official said on Monday.
The detainees belong to Tu Do Vietnam, or Free Vietnam, a U.S.-based group that seeks to overthrow the Vietnamese government, said the immigration official, who asked not to be named.
The official said the 28 Vietnamese attempted to enter Thailand illegally on Saturday via Poipet, a border town in northwest Cambodia.
They are being detained at Pochentong Airport in Phnom Penh, the official said.

One of the Vietnamese is an American citizen, an official at the U.S. embassy confirmed. The official said the embassy was in contact with the American, but added no further details on the individual's identity.

In December 1995, seven people said by the government to be members of Tu Do Vietnam were deported to Vietnam from Cambodia, and in March this year, 13 other members entered U.S. embassy grounds in Phnom Penh to seek protection.
They eventually left the compound after U.S. embassy officials persuaded them to leave.

An official at the U.S. embassy said on Monday: "The U.S. government does not in any way support or encourage these groups because we have diplomatic relations with both Vietnam and Cambodia. We don't support any group trying to overthrow the Vietnamese government."
Government estimates of the number of Tu Do Vietnam members in Cambodia has varied from several hundred to several thousand, and the Vietnamese embassy said it did not have an estimate.
"We are strongly against anti-Vietnamese government groups both in Cambodia and in other countries," a spokesman for the Vietnamese embassy told Reuters.

"There have been cases of Tu Do Vietnamese in Cambodia, so we asked the Cambodian government to help locate them, and we received a positive response," the official said, adding that he was awaiting information on the Vietnamese captured in Poipet.
